summary.one_liner: LocalGPT is a self-hosted, privacy-focused document Q&A platform that indexes PDFs, DOCX, HTML, Markdown and TXT files and answers questions about them using local Ollama models, LanceDB hybrid search and a cross-encoder reranker.
summary.what_it_does: The project parses documents with Docling (with an OCR fallback for PDFs lacking a text layer), chunks them, and optionally enriches chunks with LLM-generated context and per-document overviews. Retrieval combines dense vector search with LanceDB full-text search, fused by Reciprocal Rank Fusion and reranked by a cross-encoder (on by default). A router chooses between RAG and a direct LLM answer per query, and query decomposition splits complex questions into sub-questions. It exposes a backend gateway on port 8000 and a RAG API on port 8001 with SSE streaming, plus a Next.js web UI, a CLI, and session/index management with SQLite chat history. Optional features such as late chunking, answer verification and multi-vector retrieval are off by default, according to the README's measured evaluations.
use_cases: chat with my private PDFs offline
summarise and query internal documents without cloud uploads
build a local document Q&A index for a team
keep sensitive files on my own machine while using an LLM
prototype a RAG backend via REST API
compare retrieval configurations with the included eval harness
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd localGPT
curl -fsSL (install Ollama) && ollama pull qwen3.5:9b && ollama pull qwen3.5:4b
notable: Hybrid search fusing vector and LanceDB full-text results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, with a calibrated cross-encoder reranker
Smart router that picks between RAG retrieval and a direct LLM answer per query
Query decomposition that pools sub-question retrieval results for one rerank and synthesis pass
Documented evaluation harness and decision records explaining why each default is set
Fully local operation: models run through Ollama and embeddings from HuggingFace
caveats: The RAG API is single-threaded, so only one chat or indexing run is served at a time
Requires substantial resources: 8GB+ RAM (16GB+ recommended), and the reranker model is about 7.5 GB
Changing the embedding model invalidates existing indexes, which must be rebuilt
